lead.title: Xbrane completes enrollment in the pivotal trial of its Opdivo (nivolumab) biosimilar in melanoma
lead.deck: About 340 melanoma patients are enrolled for Xdivane, a biosimilar candidate to Bristol Myers Squibb's nivolumab (roughly $10B in 2025 Opdivo sales). Co-developer Intas runs clinical development and its arm Accord Healthcare will handle global commercialization.

milestone.title: BioNTech's mRNA vaccine BNT113 misses its first objective in HPV16+ head and neck cancer; trial continues on overall survival
milestone.summary: Combined with Keytruda in first line, BNT113 did not extend progression-free survival at an interim check; a monitoring committee recommends continuing to test overall survival.
milestone.why: Analysts saw thin supporting evidence at the start. BioNTech is refocusing oncology on the bispecific pumitamig (with Bristol Myers Squibb): a reminder of the clinical risk of therapeutic mRNA vaccines.

deal.thesis: Zealand Pharma licenses AI-engineered multispecific proteins for obesity and metabolic disease: $30M upfront, up to $35M in preclinical milestones and nearly $1.2B in milestones across two programs (option on a third), plus royalties. One more comparable for AI protein design, not an entry opportunity.

brefsEurope.title: Alvotech and Advanz file AVT29, an 8 mg Eylea biosimilar, in Europe
brefsEurope.summary: The filing targets a copy of the 8 mg Eylea dose, which the partners call a first; Alvotech takes an early lead in the race for this biosimilar.

brefsIntl.title: Arrowhead: subcutaneous RNAi ARO-MAPT cuts tau by 40–73% on average in healthy volunteers
brefsIntl.summary: Early trial in about 64 volunteers (three doses); mild side effects. Trials are planned in frontotemporal dementia and progressive supranuclear palsy; tau remains debated as an Alzheimer's target.

brefsIntl.title: Takeda spinout Cerevance reports Phase 3 data for solengepras in Parkinson's: −0.61 h daily "off" time
brefsIntl.summary: 341 patients; modest effect at the high dose, "on"-time benefit only barely significant. A meeting with the FDA is planned to define next steps.

word.definition: AI models generate protein sequences (antibodies, mini-binders, enzymes) from scratch to meet a specification, instead of screening existing libraries.

how.t: Define the target and desired properties (affinity, stability, low immunogenicity).
The model proposes thousands of candidates, ranked by in silico prediction.
The best are produced and tested in the lab, and the results retrain the model.

word.why: The VC signal: big pharma is already paying upfronts (Zealand → Generate, $30M) for access to these platforms; the open question is whether AI really shortens the path to a clinical candidate.

startups.name: Cradle
startups.use: AI protein engineering software; $73M Series B led by IVP; named customers include Novo Nordisk and J&J Innovative Medicine.

startups.name: Latent Labs
startups.use: Latent-X and Latent-X2 models (mini-binders, antibodies); $50M raised including a $40M Series A co-led by Radical Ventures and Sofinnova Partners.

startups.name: Generate Biomedicines
startups.use: AI-designed protein platform; GB-0895 (anti-TSLP) in Phase 3 for severe asthma; Nasdaq-listed (GENB) since February 2026 after a $400M IPO.
